description: Department within an organisation (15-100 people), one memory backend, role-based access. 17 questions, ~8 min to complete.

questions.prompt: What should I call this AugmentIQ setup? (e.g., 'acme-marketing-dept', 'finance-2026')
questions.why_we_ask: Used for the timeline prefix, config filename, and the department tag on every record.

questions.prompt: Which department? (e.g., marketing, finance, engineering, sales, HR, legal)
questions.why_we_ask: Used to scope records by department. Records tagged with this department are visible to members of this department (if RBAC is enabled).
questions.validation: one of: marketing, finance, engineering, sales, hr, legal, operations, product, customer_success, other

questions.prompt: How many people are in this department?
questions.why_we_ask: Used to size the cron retention window and the audit log.

questions.prompt: Which memory backend are you using?
questions.why_we_ask: For departments, Custom (AugmentIQ+ MCP server) is the recommended choice for serious use — local-first, no vendor lock-in, tamper-evident audit. mem0 is the cloud alternative.
questions.validation: one of: mem0, custom, obsidian, reme, hermes_native

options.label: Hermes native — only if everyone is on Hermes

questions.prompt: Where is the memory backend located?
questions.why_we_ask: The Skill needs the path or URL.
questions.validation: filesystem path or URL; leave blank for auto-detect

questions.why_we_ask: Drives the retention defaults and the DSR workflow. For most departments, GDPR (if EU data) + SOC2 (if audit-bound) is the default.
questions.validation: each entry one of: gdpr, soc2, hipaa, iso27001, pci_dss

questions.prompt: Default classification for this department's records?
questions.why_we_ask: Records from this department default to this classification. PII auto-upgrades to 'restricted' automatically. Lower classifications ('public', 'internal') are opt-in per record.
questions.validation: one of: public, internal, confidential, restricted

questions.prompt: Who is the DPO for DSR notifications?
questions.why_we_ask: When a DSR is fulfilled, the DPO is notified. Leave blank to skip.
Defaults: 7 years for public/internal/confidential, 3 years for restricted. Override per your retention policy. Note: GDPR requires 'no longer than necessary' — set shorter for personal data.
For departments, full cron set (daily, weekly, monthly, quarterly, on-event) is typical. Manual-only is too sparse for department-level memory.
All 7 triggers are recommended for departments. The agent auto-detects which events are available from the host agent's event sources.
questions.validation: each entry one of: commit, decision, customer_interaction, incident, policy_change, hire, contract

questions.prompt: Do you have historical data to bring in?
questions.why_we_ask: Departments typically have years of data. Yes is the default; you can skip with no if you're starting fresh.

questions.prompt: If yes, list the sources. (Agent will route enterprise platforms to customdev@upsurge.ae for paid migration.)
questions.why_we_ask: Per source, the agent will detect, classify by category, and route accordingly.
questions.validation: each entry: source_id, source_type, source_category, location, classification_default

questions.prompt: Default batch size for nightly ingest batches?
questions.why_we_ask: Per source, the agent computes a recommended batch size from volume. This is the default if the volume doesn't force a different choice.
questions.validation: one of: small_100, medium_1000, large_10000, xl_100000

questions.why_we_ask: For departments, RBAC is recommended. Members of the department can read all department records; the department head can write; the legal team can redact.

questions.prompt: Multi-agent federation? (Allow subagents to spawn for batch processing)
questions.why_we_ask: For departments, subagents are useful for large legacy ingests (batches of 10k+ records). For most department use, single-agent is sufficient.

What should AugmentIQ do if the memory backend goes down? pause_and_alert: stop writes, alert the user, resume when back. continue_silently: log and continue (records lost). abort: terminate all operations. Default is the safest.
